predictions.question: R&D gap S3.1/S3.2 (BOM): what single-ion detection efficiency eta does an IBIC counted-implantation detector reach for 10 keV P ions, as a function of detector capacitance, against the Exp67 requirement eta>=0.9 (target 0.99)?

model.signal: Ionization energy fraction (Lindhard-scale, registered assumption) 0.4 of 10 keV -> E_ion=4 keV; e-h pair creation 3.6 eV -> mean signal S electrons, Gaussian spread sigma_sig/S=0.15 (damage/straggle fluctuation, assumption).
model.noise: Charge-sensitive amplifier ENC(C) = 50 + 25*C[pF] electrons rms (registered model). Detection threshold at 5 sigma_noise; eta = Phi((S - 5*ENC)/sigma_sig). Capacitances {0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 2, 5} pF (small pixel diode to large-area diode).
model.energies: Also 5 keV and 20 keV with ionization fractions 0.35/0.45 (assumptions).

predictions.success_rule: eta >= 0.99 is reachable at 10 keV for some detector capacitance <= 0.5 pF.
predictions: AU1 SMALL PIXEL WINS: eta >= 0.99 at 10 keV for C=0.5 pF.
AU2 LARGE DIODE FAILS SPEC: eta < 0.9 at 10 keV for C=5 pF.
AU3 ENERGY HELPS: eta(20 keV) >= eta(10 keV) >= eta(5 keV) at C=0.5 pF.
AU4 THRESHOLD ROBUSTNESS: At C=0.5 pF, 10 keV, eta stays >= 0.95 even with threshold raised to 8 sigma_noise.
